correctness.rationale: Finite theorem: the five graph-order classes comprise exactly 1,2,4,11,34 unlabeled simple graphs. Independent exact code generated all 52 and evaluated every directed-linear-forest face and integer Smith boundary; only seven-edge triangular B3 (canonical mask 127) has torsion, with f=(14,54,60,12), SNF(d1)=1^13, SNF(d2)=1^40 2, SNF(d3)=1^12. Separately independently reconstructed the 140-face Morse complex: 65 distinct unit-pivot pair cancellations, 336 poset covers, complete topological acyclicity, critical cells (1,1,8) in dimensions (0,1,2), integer degree vector (0,0,0,-2,0,0,-2,0). Its two-cell degrees reduce over GL8(Z) to (2,0^7), yielding RP^2 wedge seven S^2, not merely identical homology. Scope strictly symmetric digraphs of simple graphs on <=5 ordinary vertices, not arbitrary digraphs or isolated RP2.
residual_risks: Computational corroboration is restricted to the stated finite class; it is not a general numerical experiment proof.
